_source: OpV-A2 (docs/eras/opv.md, 'A2. Circuits', process lines 11-18): the steps of the OpV circuit lines that run on GTM's cutter and assembler and on LuV's helium refrigerator. Every other step is a row of an older machine, marked OpV-A2 in its own file (the 'older rows' of the contract).
_how_it_is_used: Read by server_scripts/grindless/opv/circuits.js at every server load. Each entry of types.<type>.recipes becomes one gtceu:<type> recipe, id grindless:<type>/<name>.

itemsIn / itemsOut: { id, count, chance? } (a chance below 10 000 makes a chanced output); fluidsIn / fluidsOut: { id, amount } in mB. eut x duration. cutter and assembler are GTM's types: circuit 0 = none.

closed_loop_cooling (LuV's helium refrigerator) is keyed by its one item input and takes no circuit: the script adds the refrigerator's own make-up, pre-cool and charge (tables/helium_refrigerator.json) and its EMI line, as the generated rows have.

Destinations: the dies, the interposer, the optical link and the amplifier go to the UEV photonic integration hall (c8, gtnn:cosmic_mainframe); the InP scrap goes back to indium in EV's extraction cascade (c26). The cutter's water is used up (GTM's cutter rule).

recipes._why: line 12: the Fe-doped (semi-insulating) InP boule sawn into wafers; the kerf and the ends go to the InP scrap
recipes.name: si_inp_wafers

recipes._why: line 13: the metallised cryo-CMOS wafer diced into dies, still untested at 4 K
recipes.name: untested_cryo_cmos_dies

recipes._why: line 16: the isolated HEMT wafer diced into cryogenic low-noise amplifiers; the edge goes to the InP scrap
recipes.name: hemt_amplifiers

recipes._why: line 12: the InAs/Al wafer capped with an annealed hBN film, the gate dielectric of the 2DEG, by dry transfer: a polycarbonate stamp on a PDMS (silicone rubber) block, carried on a glass slide, picks the film up and melts it down onto the wafer, then chloroform dissolves the stamp (GTM's assembler takes one fluid)
recipes.name: hbn_capped_2deg_wafer

recipes._why: line 13: each cryo-CMOS die tested at 4 K in the refrigerator's helium loop before it is used
recipes.name: opv_cryo_cmos_die_test

recipes._why: line 14: the bonded interposer cooled below niobium's 9.2 K so every via is checked superconducting
recipes.name: opv_nb_tsv_interposer_test
